claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Differential element diffusion during cooling controls phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Cr and Al diffuse faster than Co, Fe, and Ni during cooling of this alloy.
Differential diffusion produces local compositional clustering and short-range ordering.
Local concentration fluctuations act as precursors to nucleation of secondary ordered phases.
Diffusion-generated compositional inhomogeneities create regions that energetically favor ordered structures such as B2.
Formation of an ordered secondary phase can leave a remaining disordered BCC matrix.
Slow cooling or intermediate-temperature isothermal holding provides sufficient time for diffusion and short-range ordering.
Slowly cooled or isothermally held samples should contain more secondary ordered phase and local ordering than a rapidly quenched baseline.
Rapid quenching should preserve a comparatively homogeneous, single-phase BCC structure with minimal segregation or ordering.
Ultrafast cooling suppresses the proposed mechanism by effectively freezing atomic mobility.
The mechanism should dominate only below a critical cooling rate that permits differential diffusion and short-range ordering.
After prolonged high-temperature exposure, equilibration should supersede the proposed non-equilibrium diffusion-and-ordering mechanism.
